data: The engine that launched the first American — Freedom 7
Engine registry (PRD-032). Public-source nominal specs; NASA imagery.
The engine that launched the first American into space

On 5 May 1961, Alan Shepard rode a Mercury-Redstone rocket to an altitude of 187 kilometres and back — making him the first American in space — and the engine that lifted him was the Rocketdyne A-7. Derived from the A-6 that powered the Redstone ballistic missile, the A-7 ran a gas-generator cycle on LOX and ethyl alcohol: the same propellant pairing that traced back through Redstone to the German V-2. Shepard's Freedom 7 flight lasted fifteen minutes and changed the political calculus of the Space Race. The A-7 flew only on Mercury-Redstone missions, retiring in May 1963.
